propositions: Op-cert signing material must be bound at startup from exactly one source (REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY), validated before queue/worker/network/workspace creation, and rejected if missing, both-set, unreadable, non-regular, malformed, encrypted, or non-Ed25519.

The validated key must be copied to a process-owned 0700 directory with 0600 file permissions, never modified during process lifetime, observing replacement only on restart, and cleanup must never alter the deployment source.

Both signing producer chains (completion: sign_completion_verdict→signing.sign_manifest; plan-review: generation.sign_manifest via attest.py) must accept and use an optional context-local OpcertSigner binding when supplied by the service, while developer-local callers without binding retain env/genesis resolution.

The op-cert application runtime must have no SSM, boto3, AWS region, or key-parameter runtime dependencies; the key must be materialized before startup by fetch-secrets.sh to a 0600 file and bind-mounted read-only with REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH.
Concurrent and timed-out jobs must demonstrate context-local isolation of signer, principal, and push policy with one immutable startup signer and no workspace push remote.
Secret and key material must not appear in repr, serialization, argv, logs, exceptions, output, fingerprints, provenance, child processes, or persisted envelopes.
